text:
cheng: FYI we just hit a weird tail latency regression on canary GPUs after the kernel selector change.
cheng: p95 looks stable but p99 jumped ~18% for short-seq workloads (<=128). logs attached inline.
sam: when did the selector change go out? which kernels are we choosing now?
maria: pushed v2.4.1 last night — default prefers fused-attn-xla for seq<=128 and fallback to attn-ref for long sequences. rollout was 60% traffic.
eli: repro steps from profiling: run bench_smallseq.sh with 8K qps for 2m, observe p99 climb
eli: perfbot reported a spike during the 00:30-01:10 window, coincides with a microbatch sampler change.
perfbot: nightly-regression: model=rw-13b; metric=p99; delta=+18%; window=00:28-01:12; commit=7f3a9c2
ops: can you paste the flame graph snippet? curious if it's kernel glibc or our kv-path.
cheng: here's the hot path we saw (trimmed):
```
  35%  fused-attn-xla::compute
  22%  kv-cache::apply_prefetch
  18%  fused-attn-xla::kv_index_load
  10%  cuda_memcpy_async
```
sam: kv-cache prefetch at 22% is suspicious — we changed prefetch window to 16 tokens last week.
eli: right — prefetch window shrink -> more frequent refills -> more small memcpy ops -> kernel stalls under microbatching.
maria: interesting, on Dedicated we target higher GPU util (84%) vs Hosted (72%). maybe the selector assumes microbatch sizes that don't match traffic.
devex: quickly summarizing the tradeoff we discussed: larger microbatches -> better throughput but increases p99 for short sequences; smaller microbatches -> lower utilization and cost but tighter p99.
ops: what's the canary config currently? are we using adaptive batching or fixed microbatch size?
cheng: canary had adaptive batching enabled with target_batch_ms=7, max_microbatch=8. earlier we were using static microbatch=4.
sam: sequencing: the kernel selector introduced a preference for fused-attn-xla when estimated batch_size >=6 because it outperforms for throughput. with adaptive batching, the estimator overshot frequently.
eli: that makes sense — estimator bias + prefetch window change = amplified tail.
perfbot: note: regression appears only under headroom pressure scenarios (utilization >=79%) and with KV miss rate >12%.
maria: do we have a quick sim to reproduce? ops, can you spin a 4-GPU pod with controlled kv miss pattern?
ops: spinning now. test command I used:
```
./ci/loadgen --model rw-13b --qps 8000 --seq 64 --microbatch 8 --kv-miss-rate 0.15 --duration 300
```
ops: started at 2145679200; attaching logs when done.
eli: while we wait, a hypothesis: fused-attn-xla has a higher variance for tiny KV refills due to internal tiling; attn-ref is slower on average but more predictable -> better p99 when KV churns.
cheng: agree. two short-term fixes:
- revert kernel selector rule for small-seq workloads (force attn-ref when kv_miss_rate>10% or est_batch<8)
- adjust prefetch window back to 32 tokens to reduce refill frequency
sam: longer-term: we need a cost function for kernel selection that includes p99 penalty, not just throughput. maybe use a weighted objective: cost = alpha*throughput + beta*p99_penalty.
maria: +1. Also need better signals from KV cache telemetry into the estimator: kv_miss_rate, memcpy_count, avg_prefetch_size.
devex: can we add a quick probe: when estimator is about to pick fused-attn-xla, run a microprobe (2ms) to sample memcpy and choose accordingly? cheap custom check.
eli: microprobe idea is neat but adds latency overhead; maybe run only when headroom<10% and candidate kernels differ in variance.
ops: test finished. confirming p99 +20% for the canary run when selector preferred fused-attn-xla. raw log snippet:
```
[2145679301] p95=48ms p99=162ms util=81% kv_miss=0.17 microb=8
[2145679421] p95=50ms p99=170ms util=83% kv_miss=0.18 microb=7-9 (adaptive)
```
maria: thanks. let's push a hotfix: rollback selector tweak and restore prefetch window to 32 on canary only.
sam: I'll open a rollback PR and tag perf/eng-sre. also enqueue a canary run with forced attn-ref for seq<=128.
cheng: after rollback we should run a controlled A/B: attn-ref vs fused-attn-xla with identical microbatching and kv-miss pattern to measure p95/p99 and throughput delta.
eli: make sure to surface memory-copy counts and memcpy latency distribution in the comparison.
perfbot: perf-test-scheduled: test_id=pt-2145680400, tags=[canary, rollback, kvprobe]
devex: we should also add a small change to our kernel picker to penalize kernels with high memcpy variance. sample code sketch:
```
score = throughput_score - lambda * memcpy_variance_penalty
if score(fused) < score(attn_ref): pick attn_ref
```
sam: agree; lambda can be tuned from historical runs.
ops: let's target rollback deploy in 20m to limit customer impact.
cheng: also file a follow-up issue to audit microbatch estimator—it's overly optimistic when prefetch window small.
maria: created issue #ENG-1142: "kernel selector sensitivity to kv-prefetch and estimator bias" and assigned to sam/eli.
eli: TL;DR: root cause likely interaction between prefetche window shrink + estimator bias + kernel variance -> p99 spikes under high util. Hotfix: rollback kernel rule + increase prefetch window -> run AB test -> instrument memcpy variance -> add penalty in selector.
sam: sounds good. thanks all. :thumbsup:
devex: /cc product for visibility — this explains a small but noticeable latency blip in hosted metrics last night.
perfbot: note: will re-run nightly after rollback and post updated deltas.
